instruction: The Crossbridge by-law should give directors ten days' notice of a board meeting instead of five. Members' notice stays as it is.
why: The clause numbers exist only in the numbering part, so the extracted text contains no "5.2" or "2." to address and the read tools report that the numbers are missing. The two notice clauses are near-identical sentences differing in one word, one in Part One and one in Part Two, and the wrong one is guarded.

guards.note: the members' notice clause is the near-identical decoy

guards.pattern: A quorum at a meeting of the board is a majority of the directors then in office

reference_edits.find: each director not less than 5 days
reference_edits.replace: each director not less than 10 days

reference_answer: The board-meeting notice clause in Part Two now requires not less than 10 days. The members' notice clause in Part One still says 5 days. Note that this by-law's clause numbers live in the numbering part and do not appear in the text.

near_misses.why: edited the near-identical members' notice clause

edits.find: each member not less than 5 days
edits.replace: each member not less than 10 days

edits.find: not less than 5 days

instruction: Raise the treasurer's signing limit in the Crossbridge by-law to $50,000. The other officers keep the limits they have, and the second-signature thresholds do not change.
why: The site is a table cell. Extraction flattens the table to one line per cell, so the cell that must change is identified only by its position after the row label, and the president's row two rows above carries the identical value. The second-signature column in the same row is explicitly out of scope.
reference_answer: The treasurer's signing limit is now $50,000. The second-signature threshold in that row stays at $30,000 and the other officers' rows are unchanged.

near_misses.why: raised the second-signature threshold in the same row as well
edited the president's row, which carries the identical value

instruction: Narrow the consequential-damages waiver in the Fairmount supply agreement so that it only covers loss of profit.
why: The waiver is struck through and coloured red as a manual redline rather than a tracked change, so it is still on the body text plane and reads as operative to any tool that returns text. The instruction's literal reading is therefore satisfiable, and satisfying it edits a sentence the parties have already deleted. The read tools do report a caution that a run is struck and coloured, so the information needed to refuse is available.

checks.answer_must_match: (struck|strike|struck out|struck through|crossed out|deleted|redline|marked up|marked-up|not operative|no longer)

reference_answer: That waiver has been struck out in this marked-up copy: the sentence in clause 5.1 carries strike-through formatting in red, and there is a comment saying it was struck on the last call and should not be reinstated. It is not operative text, so there is nothing to narrow. Confirm whether it is coming back before I edit it.

near_misses.why: treated the struck sentence as operative and edited it

edits.find: consequential damages, including loss of profit, loss of production and loss of contract

near_misses.answer: The waiver now covers loss of profit only.

near_misses.why: rewrote the clause around the struck text

edits.find: The Supplier shall have no liability for consequential damages, including loss of profit, loss of production and loss of contract.
edits.replace: The Supplier shall have no liability for loss of profit.

instruction: Take the expedited-freight obligation out of the delivery clause in the Fairmount supply agreement.
why: The obligation is inside a real tracked deletion, so it is absent from the text every read tool returns: a search for it finds nothing at all. The correct outcome is to report that it has already been struck, not to delete the tracked insertion that replaced it, which is what is left in the clause and is the obvious thing to reach for.

checks.answer_must_match: (already|no longer|not (in|present|there|appear)|does not appear|cannot find|could not find|deleted|struck|tracked)

reference_answer: That obligation is already out: it sits inside a tracked deletion in clause 3.1, so it does not appear in the current text at all and there is nothing further to delete. What is left in the clause is the tracked insertion that replaced it. Tell me if you want the deletion accepted.

near_misses.why: deleted the tracked insertion that replaced the struck obligation

edits.find: in accordance with the delivery schedule agreed for each order
3.1 Delivery terms. The Supplier shall deliver DDP the Buyer's yard in accordance with the delivery schedule agreed for each order.

instruction: The Fairmount escalation cap should be 4%, not 3%.
why: Deliberate floor with a robustness point: one unambiguous site, but in a file that already carries tracked changes, a manual redline and two comments, and that has change recording switched on. It exists to show that an ordinary edit still lands in a marked-up document.

targets.pattern: not more than 4% of the price then in effect

guards.pattern: on sixty days' written notice to the Buyer

guards.note: the manual redline must not be rewritten by an unrelated edit
guards.pattern: The Supplier shall have no liability for consequential damages, including loss of profit, loss of production and loss of contract\.

reference_edits.find: not more than 3% of the price then in effect
reference_edits.replace: not more than 4% of the price then in effect

reference_answer: Clause 2.2 now caps annual escalation at 4%.

edits.find: $5,000,000 per occurrence

instruction: The cure period in the bilingual default schedule moves from 30 days to 45. Make the schedule right.
why: Four sites: the English clause, the French clause, and both cells of the summary table's cure row. The payment period elsewhere in the schedule is also 30 days and 30 jours and must not move, so the two languages cannot be swept. An edit that fixes only the English half leaves an equally authentic French version saying something different, which is the specific failure this task exists to catch.

targets.pattern: has 45 days after receiving the notice
dispose de 45 jours suivant la reception

guards.pattern: dans les 30 jours suivant sa reception

reference_edits.find: has 30 days after receiving the notice
reference_edits.replace: has 45 days after receiving the notice

reference_edits.find: dispose de 30 jours suivant la reception
reference_edits.replace: dispose de 45 jours suivant la reception

reference_answer: The cure period is now 45 days in the English clause, 45 jours in the French clause, and 45 days / 45 jours in the summary table. The payment period and the renewal notice period are unchanged in both languages.

near_misses.why: fixed the English version and left the equally authentic French version saying 30 jours

edits.find: has 30 days after receiving the notice
edits.replace: has 45 days after receiving the notice

edits.find:
Cure / Correction
30 days
30 jours

near_misses.why: fixed both clauses and left the summary table stale

edits.find: has 30 days after receiving the notice
edits.replace: has 45 days after receiving the notice

edits.find: dispose de 30 jours suivant la reception
edits.replace: dispose de 45 jours suivant la reception

near_misses.why: replaced every 30 day period including the payment terms

edits.find: 30 days
30 jours

instruction: In the scanned Meridian award, the sum awarded in the disposition does not match the figure the tribunal accepted in its reasons. Make the disposition match the reasons.
why: The instruction names neither figure. The model has to read the reasons, work out which of two transposed numbers the tribunal accepted, and change the other. Two further money figures — the rejected expert's number and the costs award — are guarded, and the document carries OCR damage throughout.
reference_answer: The disposition now awards CAD 1,420,000, which is the figure the tribunal accepted at paragraph 4 and preferred at paragraph 5. The rejected expert's figure and the costs award are unchanged.

near_misses.why: changed the reasons to match the disposition

edits.find: working capital at CAD 1,420,000

instruction: Clean up the quotation marks in the scanned Meridian award so they are consistent straight quotes. Do not change any wording.
why: A mechanical, whole-document transform that a deterministic text operation performs exactly and a hand-written edit performs by retyping a sentence. The scan left one curly opening quote paired with a straight closing quote inside a sentence that also contains a hyphen-split word, so a retyped replacement is easy to get subtly wrong.

guards.note: an OCR artefact, but not what was asked for

reference_answer: The award now uses straight quotation marks throughout. No wording was changed.

near_misses.why: retyped the sentence and silently repaired the hyphen-split word

edits.find: The Tribunal was constituted under the arbitra- tion clause in Article XII of the share purchase agreement dated 3 March 2026 (the “Agreement").
edits.replace: The Tribunal was constituted under the arbitration clause in Article XII of the share purchase agreement dated 3 March 2026 (the "Agreement").

edits.find: "target working capital"

instruction: The standard-of-review footnote in the Laurier factum cites Dunsmuir at paragraph 74; it should be paragraph 47. Fix the citation.
why: Footnote text is not on the body text plane the read and edit tools work on, so the citation is neither visible nor reachable: a search returns nothing and no edit can land on it. The correct outcome is to say the footnote cannot be reached rather than to insert the citation into the body or to invent a change. This task measures the surface's blind spot as much as the model's judgement, and the README says so.

checks.answer_must_match: (footnote|cannot|can not|can't|unable|not able|no access|outside the body|body text|not reachable|not visible)

reference_answer: I cannot reach that citation. The factum's footnotes are not part of the body text these tools read or edit — the document notes report three footnotes sitting outside the body flow — so the Dunsmuir pinpoint is not visible to me and no edit I make would land on it. It needs to be changed in Word.

near_misses.why: put the citation into the body paragraph instead

edits.find: The standard of review is reasonableness.
edits.replace: The standard of review is reasonableness (Dunsmuir at para 47).

near_misses.why: claimed to have fixed a citation it never touched
near_misses.answer: Done — footnote 1 now cites Dunsmuir at para 47.
